title: Zero pairwise failure correlations leave half-weight loss uncertain in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested whether contact sizes and pairwise independent failures fix the chance of losing at least half of cleft-weighted input. We used verified published contact tables from Allen V1 Deep Dive and MICrONS. We selected 1,512 and 1,438 connections with three through eight observed contacts. Each contact had an assumed failure probability of 0.1. Exact finite-state linear programs left a nonzero probability range in 1,013 and 904 connections. Mean ranges were 0.03935 to 0.05507 and 0.04294 to 0.05888. Full-independence means were 0.05069 and 0.05312. All allowed laws have the same weighted mean and variance. Checks of primal and dual solutions, exact three-contact laws, scalar enumeration, and a repeated run supported the calculations. This extends earlier count-based silence bounds to size-weighted loss in two maps. It uses an established method. Assumed failure rates, one animal per map, size as a proxy, incomplete arbors, and no release measurements limit biological claims. Code, aggregate results, provenance, and verified external-input retrieval steps are supplied.

display.caption: Mean sharp bounds on half-weight loss with 10 percent contact failure and pairwise independence. Black points show full independence. Bands are model ranges, not confidence intervals.
